jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is searching for an Early Career Geologist to support our San Francisco, CA
, San Jose, CA
or Oakland, CA
office.

As an Entry Level Geologist, you will work with multi-disciplinary teams on site characterization and remediation projects including hydrogeologic and environmental data collection; routine groundwater monitoring programs; remedial investigations and feasibility study analyses (e.g. soil characterization to delineate environmental excavations or pilot testing to inform in-situ remediation design); and data evaluation and management. These tasks include both technical writing and analysis. This position requires travel to field assignments about 25-50% of the time. All work performed within this position will be under the close supervision of the project manager or more senior personnel.

Your Impact

Under general supervision, perform routine field activities associated with environmental site investigations and remediation projects, including soil, groundwater, soil vapor, sediment, and surface water sampling, drilling oversight, monitoring well installation, and remediation system support.
Maintain quality assurance and quality control procedures to ensure accurate sample collection, documentation, and data integrity.
Generate complete, accurate, and concise field documentation using electronic data collection systems, field logs, and project records.
Comply with all health, safety, and site-specific requirements, including sample handling protocols, chain-of-custody procedures, equipment decontamination, and environmental regulations.
Support the preparation of technical memoranda, field reports, and environmental data summaries.
Utilize current technologies and industry best practices to support environmental investigations, contaminant characterization, and remediation efforts.
Complete required training and certifications necessary to support field and project assignments.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company resources and conduct while adhering to WSP's Code of Conduct and related policies.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science or a closely related discipline.
0 to 1 years of related work experience.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and research skills.
Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated attention to detail, organization, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic project environment.
Ability to work independently under general supervision and collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Proficiency with technical writing, Microsoft Office applications, and environmental data management tools.
Proven commitment to workplace safety and ability to comply with WSP's health, safety, drug/alcohol, and harassment policies.
Ability to perform fieldwork in varying weather and site conditions and work schedules conducive to project requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
Valid driver's license and willingness to travel as required to support project needs.
OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification or ability to obtain certification.
Ability to pursue Professional Geologist registration in California.

Preferred Qualifications

Mater's Degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science or a closely related discipline.
Previous internship, coursework, or experience related to environmental site investigations, remediation, due diligence, or contaminated site management.
Experience with groundwater monitoring, drilling oversight, remediation system operations, or environmental data evaluation.
Active participation in professional organizations related to geology, hydrogeology, environmental science, or remediation.

WSP Benefits:

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation:

Expected Salary: $63,000 - $78,700

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

to support utility infrastructure documentation and field data collection services using various field data capture tools and related reality capture platforms
. This position is responsible for capturing high-quality geospatial imagery, utility asset data, and field observations to support engineering, construction, utility mapping, and asset management projects.

The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, comfortable working outdoors, around vehicular traffic, and interested in technology-driven field operations. This is an entry-level to early-career position with opportunities for advancement in engineering, design, surveying, and project management.

Operate scanning and reality capture equipment to collect utility asset and infrastructure data.
Capture georeferenced imagery and field documentation for utility, telecommunications, transportation, and civil infrastructure projects.
Perform field data collection activities along utility corridors, rights-of-way, roadways, and construction sites.
Verify asset locations and document field conditions using mobile applications and GIS-enabled platforms.
Upload, organize, and maintain project data in accordance with company quality standards.
Assist senior field staff with utility investigations, site assessments, and infrastructure documentation.
Record measurements, field notes, photographs, and observations during project activities.
Support utility mapping and asset inventory projects through accurate data capture and reporting.
Interpreted utility mapping records and as-builts
Perform routine equipment inspections, maintenance, and operational checks.
Adhere to company safety policies, local regulations, and project-specific requirements.
Maintain communication with project managers and field supervisors regarding project progress and field conditions.
Adhere and work around traffic control setup and site safety procedures when required.

Requirements

High school diploma or GED required.
0–2 years of field operations, utility services, construction, surveying, telecommunications, or related experience.
Ability to operate mobile technology, tablets, smartphones, and cloud-based applications.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Excellent organizational and communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a field team.
Valid driver's license with acceptable driving record.
Ability to travel to project sites as required.

Preferred Qualifications

Associate degree in Engineering Technology, Geomatics, Construction Management, GIS, or related field preferred.
Experience with utility locating, surveying, or infrastructure documentation.
Familiarity with GPS/GNSS data collection equipment.
Experience working in utility, telecommunications, construction, or engineering environments.
Knowledge of underground utility infrastructure and utility safety practices.

Physical Requirements

Ability to walk long distances across varying terrain.
Ability to work outdoors in varied weather conditions.
Ability to lift and carry equipment up to 50 lbs.
Ability to stand, bend, kneel, and perform field activities for extended periods.
Ability to safely enter active construction and utility work environments.

Work Environment

Primarily field-based position.
Frequent travel to project locations.
Work may occur near roadways, utility infrastructure, and active construction sites.
Occasional overnight travel may be required based on project needs.

The pay range for this California position is $25- $28 per hour; however, base pay offered may be higher or lower depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience of the candidate. Full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position offered. This information is provided per California Senate Bill 1162. Base pay information is based on market location. Applicants should apply via the NV5 careers site.

Benefits

NV5 offers a competitive compensation and benefits package including medical, dental, life insurance, PTO, 401(k) and professional development/advancement opportunities.

Competitive Salary
Medical, dental, and supplemental insurance
Employee Assistance Program
Company paid Life & AD&D
Company paid Disability
401K Plan
Paid Holidays
Paid Time Off

NV5 delivers technology-enabled engineering, consulting, and geospatial solutions that help clients plan, design, and optimize infrastructure, buildings, utilities, and environmental systems. We bring together technical expertise, data, and innovative thinking to create resilient, high-performance assets. As part of TiC Solutions, alongside Acuren, we share a purpose: to shape and strengthen the physical world.

Role Overview

The Quality Data Analyst turns quality data into decisions. This role analyzes the company’s quality data, including warranty return rates, customer feedback, product reviews, and factory operational KPIs, to identify trends, uncover root causes, and drive improvements in products, operational processes, and business strategy.

Working closely with Quality, Engineering, Operations, Customer Service, and Supply Chain teams, the analyst builds dashboards that give clear visibility into how current systems and products are performing, designs experiments to determine the best configurations or operational changes, and applies predictive modeling to improve customer experience, operational excellence, and other business outcomes. The analyst tracks quality performance over time and delivers clear, data-backed recommendations to stakeholders at every level of the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Data analysis and preparation

Collect, combine, and analyze quality data from multiple sources, such as warranty claims, returns and RMA records, customer service tickets, product reviews, factory inspection results, and supplier data.
Review data structures and identify errors, inconsistencies, and gaps before analysis begins.
Clean and prepare data by correcting errors, removing duplicates, and handling missing values, documenting each step so results are repeatable.
Identify trends, patterns, and outliers in failure modes, defect rates, and return reasons, and dig into the root causes behind them.

Validation and testing

Run validation checks to confirm data meets business rules and quality standards.
Build and maintain automated data quality checks so issues are caught early rather than discovered in reports.
Design and run experiments (A/B tests, process trials, design-of-experiments studies) to evaluate proposed product or operational changes and measure their impact.

Dashboard development and reporting

Develop and maintain dashboards that give leadership and cross-functional teams real-time visibility into quality performance, from the factory floor to the customer’s hands.
Automate recurring reports (weekly, monthly, and quarterly quality reviews) to reduce manual work and improve accuracy.
Translate complex findings into clear, concise summaries and visuals for both technical and non-technical audiences.

KPI monitoring and predictive analytics

Track key quality metrics such as warranty return rates, customer returns, defect rates, first-pass yield, and other operational KPIs, and flag negative trends early.
Build predictive models to forecast warranty exposure, anticipate emerging product issues, and support proactive decisions that improve customer experience and operational excellence.
Set baselines and targets for quality KPIs in partnership with Quality and Operations leadership.

Cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement

Partner with Engineering, Operations, and suppliers to investigate quality issues and support corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
Share insights from customer feedback and field returns with Product Development to inform future designs.
Provide data-driven recommendations and follow up to measure whether implemented changes delivered the expected results.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
3+ years of experience in data analytics, preferably in consumer goods, consumer electronics, or a related industry.
Strong proficiency in SQL, plus experience with a scripting or programming language (such as Python or R) for data analysis.
Hands-on experience with data visualization tools (such as Power BI or Tableau) and building dashboards for business users.
Solid knowledge of statistical techniques and concepts (regression, probability distributions, hypothesis testing and their proper use) and experience applying them to real business problems.
Experience working in a fulfillment, production, or other operational environment.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with strong attention to detail.

Preferred

Familiarity with quality tools and methodologies such as Six Sigma, Statistical Process Control (SPC), 8D, or root cause analysis.
Experience analyzing warranty, returns, or customer feedback data, including text analysis of reviews or service tickets.
Experience with predictive modeling or machine learning techniques.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment and to work independently.

Our vision is to be a global leader in improving the quality of communication for people across the lifespan and promote access and inclusion within their communities.

Position Description:

The Bilingual Research Project Coordinator reports directly to the Chair of the Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders and supports the daily coordination of research involving a new grant on the identification of language and reading disorders in 6-year-old children and communication with their families for the project LQYSQ . The coordinator develops and maintains relationships with schools, after-school programs, pediatric offices, libraries, community centers, family-serving organizations, and other local partners that can help connect eligible families with the study.

The coordinator communicates with families in English and Spanish, supports screening and enrollment, schedules study activities, maintains recruitment and participant records, coordinates research assistants and volunteers, and monitors progress toward enrollment goals. The position also supports REDCap records, IRB documentation, data quality, and general study organization. The employee must be energetic, approachable, culturally responsive, highly organized, and comfortable working independently in both office and community settings.

This position requires on-site presence and regular travel to locations within the community. The work should include regular daytime office coverage and flexibility for afternoon, evening, or occasional weekend community events, with corresponding schedule adjustments.

This position is grant funded and will be reviewed on a yearly basis.

Responsibilities

Community outreach and relationship development

Develops and maintains relationships with schools, after-school programs, libraries, pediatric offices, community centers, family-serving programs, cultural organizations, and other community partners. Represents the study at meetings, presentations, family events, health fairs, and community activities. Explains the study in English or Spanish using approved information; distributes IRB-approved materials; identifies appropriate outreach opportunities; maintains a current community contact list; and conducts professional follow-up with community partners. Travels regularly to locations throughout the region.

Family engagement, screening, and enrollment support

Communicates with interested and enrolled families in English and Spanish by telephone, email, text, video meeting, or in person. Responds to inquiries, conducts approved eligibility screening, schedules appointments, sends reminders, answers routine study questions, and supports participant retention. When appropriately trained and authorized under the IRB-approved study protocol, conducts the parental permission, child assent and assessment process. Documents family contacts accurately and maintains a welcoming, respectful, and culturally responsive experience.

Project organization and daily operations

Coordinates study calendars, participant appointments, rooms, supplies, equipment, outreach materials, and research assistant assignments. Maintains recruitment logs, participant files, REDCap records, enrollment dashboards, and weekly task lists. Tracks progress toward the study goal of 120 child-parent participants, including the English-speaking and Spanish-speaking/bilingual groups. Provides regular progress updates to the Department Chair and follows up on incomplete tasks or pending family contacts.

Research documentation, data quality, and team support

Maintains current IRB-approved recruitment, screening, consent, assent, and study materials. Enters and reviews study information, performs routine quality-control checks, protects confidential information, and follows applicable IRB, HIPAA, university, and study requirements. Provides functional guidance to research assistants and volunteers, helps organize training and assignments, and recommends practical improvements to outreach, participant tracking, and study workflow.

Performs Other Duties As Assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

Professional fluency in spoken and written English and Spanish. The employee must be able to communicate comfortably and clearly with English- and Spanish-speaking and bilingual families.
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a field related to the position’s responsibilities, such as Communication Sciences and Disorders, Public Health, Education, Psychology, Social Work, Sociology, Linguistics, Communications, Marketing, Family Studies, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience working directly with community members through employment, internships, service-learning, volunteer work, student organizations, schools, family programs, health programs, community organizations, or similar settings.
Strong interpersonal, public-speaking, relationship-building, organization, and follow-up skills.
Ability to initiate conversations, establish trust, maintain professional relationships, and represent the study positively in the community.
Ability to travel locally and work occasionally in the afternoon, evening, or weekend events as needed.
Ability to maintain confidential records and complete required research and university training.

This role is designed as an entry point for someone early in their private-service career who wants to grow into more senior portfolio work. For the right person who thrives in the role, there is a clear path to Senior Property Manager and, in the longer term, to a broader Portfolio Manager role overseeing additional properties and staff. We are looking for someone who is organized, resourceful, and eager to build a long-term career in luxury residential property management. Our ideal candidate:
Has experience coordinating residential properties, hospitality operations, facilities, or a comparable service environment.
Is highly organized and thrives on managing multiple projects, vendors, and competing priorities simultaneously.

Is solutions-oriented, persistent, and comfortable working independently while knowing when to escalate issues.

Is interested in growing into a Senior Property Manager or broader Portfolio Manager role over time.

Property & Vendor Management

Oversee all maintenance, repairs, renovations, and capital projects across the property/properties
Source, vet, schedule, and supervise contractors, vendors, and service providers (HVAC, landscaping, pool, security, smart home, cleaning, etc.)
Maintain a preventive maintenance calendar and vendor service log
Review and manage vendor invoices, contracts, and service agreements; track budgets and flag overages
Conduct regular property walkthroughs to catch issues before they become problems
Provide light-touch oversight of the Providence, RI property — coordinating seasonal opening/closing, vendor visits, and remote check-ins between site visits

Maintain a shared project/task tracker visible to relevant staff (PA, chief of staff, family office)
Anticipate needs before they become requests — flagging upcoming maintenance, seasonal prep, or potential conflicts proactively rather than waiting to be asked

Experience coordinating multiple contractors/vendors, even if not fully independent

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is searching for an Early Career Geologist to support our San Francisco, CA
, San Jose, CA
or Oakland, CA
office.

As an Entry Level Geologist, you will work with multi-disciplinary teams on site characterization and remediation projects including hydrogeologic and environmental data collection; routine groundwater monitoring programs; remedial investigations and feasibility study analyses (e.g. soil characterization to delineate environmental excavations or pilot testing to inform in-situ remediation design); and data evaluation and management. These tasks include both technical writing and analysis. This position requires travel to field assignments about 25-50% of the time. All work performed within this position will be under the close supervision of the project manager or more senior personnel.

Your Impact

Under general supervision, perform routine field activities associated with environmental site investigations and remediation projects, including soil, groundwater, soil vapor, sediment, and surface water sampling, drilling oversight, monitoring well installation, and remediation system support.
Maintain quality assurance and quality control procedures to ensure accurate sample collection, documentation, and data integrity.
Generate complete, accurate, and concise field documentation using electronic data collection systems, field logs, and project records.
Comply with all health, safety, and site-specific requirements, including sample handling protocols, chain-of-custody procedures, equipment decontamination, and environmental regulations.
Support the preparation of technical memoranda, field reports, and environmental data summaries.
Utilize current technologies and industry best practices to support environmental investigations, contaminant characterization, and remediation efforts.
Complete required training and certifications necessary to support field and project assignments.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company resources and conduct while adhering to WSP's Code of Conduct and related policies.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science or a closely related discipline.
0 to 1 years of related work experience.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and research skills.
Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated attention to detail, organization, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic project environment.
Ability to work independently under general supervision and collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Proficiency with technical writing, Microsoft Office applications, and environmental data management tools.
Proven commitment to workplace safety and ability to comply with WSP's health, safety, drug/alcohol, and harassment policies.
Ability to perform fieldwork in varying weather and site conditions and work schedules conducive to project requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
Valid driver's license and willingness to travel as required to support project needs.
OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification or ability to obtain certification.
Ability to pursue Professional Geologist registration in California.

Mater's Degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science or a closely related discipline.
Previous internship, coursework, or experience related to environmental site investigations, remediation, due diligence, or contaminated site management.

Active participation in professional organizations related to geology, hydrogeology, environmental science, or remediation.

The Senior Data Analyst is responsible for extracting, processing, analyzing, and reporting on data to produce rigorous, actionable insights and research. Drives the documentation of data and analytics needs in projects of high complexity with a student and equity-centered lens, collaborating with peers, cross-functional partners, faculty staff, and leaders.
Translates of user stories into technical requirements.
Answers complex business questions requiring extensive knowledge of the university’s data assets across several domains and departments.
Identifies adequate data sources and data sets to evaluate hypotheses, build forecasts, and support findings of research projects and experiments.
Collaborates with Data Engineering in the development of complex ETL/ELT processes and data pipelines.
Identifies, investigates, and solves complex data issues, contributing to the accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and validity of the university’s data.
Collaborates with Data Engineering and other data & analytics partners to define standards and best practices that increase data quality across the university.
Combines data analysis, visualization, and narrative structures to convey information in compelling ways that instigate deliberate action.

Creates and organizes information about processes, projects, operations, data assets, and insights from analyses and research, making it accessible in ways that increase the university’s knowledge and efficiency.
Writes and interprets technical documentation (e.g., Entity-Relationship, Conceptual, Logical, and Physical data models).
Contributes actively to the development of the university’s data management platforms (e.g., data dictionaries, catalogs, etc.).
Supports and accelerates other team members’ development through constructive feedback and sharing of technical and institutional knowledge.
Drives tasks, activities, and small-scale projects with high levels of autonomy, confidence, and collaboration with peers and partners.
Tracks and reports own progress, dependencies, and challenges diligently. Breaks down complex goals into concrete tasks and activities.
Works actively to improve own skills and knowledge through internal and external, formal and informal, structured and unstructured learning. Is a lifelong learner and embodies a growth mindset. Stays abreast of innovative developments in their area of work and plays an active role in deploying them at the university.
Understands and abides by the relevant policies and methods to access, use, transform, store, and delete data in responsible, secure, and compliant ways.
Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Advanced SQL proficiency, with experience writing queries and subqueries, modifying data, creating views, and knowledge of different join types, filtering, sorting, aggregation, window functions, common table expressions (CTE), and performance tuning.
Highly proficient and experienced in using tools like Tableau and Power BI to present data and information utilizing charts, graphs, and maps, in ways that make it easy to understand trends, patterns, and outliers.

Proficient in MS Office suite, including advanced Excel knowledge.
Proficient in flowchart and diagramming tools like Miro, Visio, Lucidchart, and similar applications.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in a related discipline

Experience

5 years of related experience in Data Analysis, Business Intelligence, Data Science, Statistics, Decision Intelligence, Research, Learning Science, or Behavioral/Cognitive Psychology.

An equivalent combination of training, experience, credentials, or accomplishments demonstrating the ability to perform the essential functions of this job may substitute for education degree requirements.

Position themselves for value-based care delivery.
Align hospitals and physician organizations.
Strengthen financial performance.
Enhance clinical programs.

Enhance existing models and capabilities built using SQL, primarily, with some use of Python or R in certain models or scenarios.
Perform complex analyses on big data, including cleaning, preparing, and interpreting.
Identify and execute analyses in response to consultant business intelligence inquiries.
Build relational databases using a Microsoft SQL Server or Fabric.
Communicate market insights to pursuit teams, and support business development efforts.
Configure, maintain, and build flexible reports, queries, and visuals within the Power BI environment and the production and development environments of related databases.
Research, test, and implement solutions in Power BI.
Partner with various consulting units (Strategy & Enterprise Growth, Payer Strategy & Contracting, Health System Performance, and Medical Group Optimization) to gather requirements related to data analytics.
Develop, configure, and maintain interfaces to exchange data among Power BI, SQL databases, and other cloud-based applications.
Create and maintain analytical support documentation and operating procedures.
Develop new and innovative methodologies and approaches.
Contribute to internal education and learning opportunities for consultants and operations members for the Analytics Hub and analytics in general, and support education about ECG’s use cases related to analytics.
Assist the vice president of data analytics and AI in developing analytics and data strategy to support data analytics capabilities at the firm.

Strong knowledge of and passion for the healthcare industry
A bachelor’s degree in either computer science, computer engineering, mathematics, statistics, health information management, or a related degree that relies heavily on critical thinking, logic, and math
5+ years of experience in healthcare data analytics, including analyzing clinical, operational, financial, or population health data
Experience in healthcare consulting, healthcare technology, or working for a hospital or health system, using data to deliver actionable insights and recommendations
Strong proficiency in data analysis, reporting, dashboard development, and translating complex data into actionable business insights
Experience working with healthcare datasets such as claims, EHRs, patient outcomes, quality metrics, or value-based care programs is highly preferred
Advanced skills in SQL and data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI); experience with Python, R, Databricks, or Azure is a plus

Excellent organizational skills

Full time/exempt

About the Role:

We are seeking a proactive, detail-oriented Residential Property Coordinator to support the day-to-day operations, maintenance, and vendor management of a portfolio of luxury private residences. Based out of a family office in Hudson Yards, this role is responsible for coordinating property operations across two Manhattan residences, with light oversight of a property in Providence, RI.

The Residential Property Coordinator will serve as the central point of coordination between contractors, vendors, household staff, and the family office to ensure properties are maintained to the highest standards. This position combines hands-on facilities coordination with administrative ownership, requiring exceptional organization, discretion, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced private household environment.

This role is designed as an entry point for someone early in their private-service career who wants to grow into more senior portfolio work. For the right person who thrives in the role, there is a clear path to Senior Property Manager and, in the longer term, to a broader Portfolio Manager role overseeing additional properties and staff. We're looking for someone who sees this as the start of a career in the industry, not just a job.

About the Candidate:

We are looking for someone who is organized, resourceful, and eager to build a long-term career in luxury residential property management. Our ideal candidate:
Has experience coordinating residential properties, hospitality operations, facilities, or a comparable service environment.
Is highly organized and thrives on managing multiple projects, vendors, and competing priorities simultaneously.
Takes ownership of their work and follows through until issues are fully resolved.
Is proactive, anticipating needs and identifying potential issues before they become problems.
Communicates professionally and confidently with principals, household staff, contractors, and vendors.
Exercises sound judgment, discretion, and professionalism in high-end residential environments.
Is solutions-oriented, persistent, and comfortable working independently while knowing when to escalate issues.
Enjoys building systems and maintaining organized records, schedules, and tracking tools.
Is interested in growing into a Senior Property Manager or broader Portfolio Manager role over time.

If this sounds like you and you believe you’d be a good fit, we strongly encourage you to apply!

Key Responsibilities:

Property & Vendor Management

Oversee all maintenance, repairs, renovations, and capital projects across the property/properties
Source, vet, schedule, and supervise contractors, vendors, and service providers (HVAC, landscaping, pool, security, smart home, cleaning, etc.)
Maintain a preventive maintenance calendar and vendor service log
Review and manage vendor invoices, contracts, and service agreements; track budgets and flag overages
Conduct regular property walkthroughs to catch issues before they become problems
Provide light-touch oversight of the Providence, RI property — coordinating seasonal opening/closing, vendor visits, and remote check-ins between site visits

Schedule & Priority Coordination

Coordinate all property access, vendor visits, and project timelines around the principal's (and family's) calendar — nothing happens in occupied spaces without sign-off
Triage and sequence competing priorities (e.g., urgent repair vs. scheduled event vs. principal's presence at the home) with sound judgment on what needs escalation vs. what can be handled independently
Maintain a shared project/task tracker visible to relevant staff (PA, chief of staff, family office)
Anticipate needs before they become requests — flagging upcoming maintenance, seasonal prep, or potential conflicts proactively rather than waiting to be asked

Portfolio Meetings & Task Management

Run weekly portfolio meetings covering the status of every property — open projects, vendor visits, maintenance items, and upcoming schedule conflicts
Maintain and distribute a master task list across the full portfolio, assigning clear owners and due dates
Follow up on outstanding action items between meetings and flag anything at risk of slipping
Summarize weekly meeting outcomes for the PA/chief of staff and principal as needed

Staff Integration

Work in close, daily coordination with the personal assistant(s) and household staff — this is not a siloed role
Coordinate closely with the Design Director on renovation, furnishing, and capital projects, ensuring vendor and contractor work aligns with design direction and timelines
Match the communication style, discretion, and professionalism standards of the existing household team
Present consistently (attire, tone, presence) with other principal-facing staff when in shared spaces or during owner visits
Participate in regular check-ins with PA/household team to align on schedules, priorities, and upcoming needs

Administrative Ownership

Own the administrative backbone of the portfolio — this is a core function of the role, not a secondary duty
Collect, verify, and track Certificates of Insurance (COIs) for every vendor and contractor prior to any site access; maintain a current COI log and proactively chase renewals before they lapse
Schedule, confirm, and track all deliveries across the portfolio, including receiving logistics, access coordination, and follow-up on delayed or missing items
Log and track all incoming requests — from the principal, PA, family office, or vendors — through to completion, with clear status visibility for the team at any given time
Maintain organized digital records: COIs, warranties, service contracts, property manuals, insurance documentation, and vendor W-9s/agreements
Keep the request/task tracker and COI log accurate and current; this is treated as a standing deliverable, not an occasional cleanup
Maintain confidentiality of all household, family, and financial information
Support ad hoc requests from the principal or PA team as needed (deliveries, special projects, event prep support)

Knowledge, Skills, and Experience:

3–5 years managing residential properties, luxury estates, or comparable private service environment (HNW/UHNW household experience a strong plus, not required)
Experience coordinating multiple contractors/vendors, even if not fully independent
Demonstrated discretion and sound judgment; comfortable in, or eager to learn, a private household setting
Strong written and verbal communication; comfortable interfacing with principals and senior staff directly
Highly organized with excellent follow-through on multi-threaded projects and task tracking
Naturally proactive, spots issues and gets ahead of them rather than waiting for direction
Solution-oriented, approaches problems by working through options rather than just flagging what's wrong
Persistent; willing to dig in and try repeatedly to solve a problem before escalating or giving up on it
Action-oriented and hands-on, a doer who takes ownership and follows through personally rather than routing things to someone else
Comfortable running structured meetings and keeping a group aligned on priorities
Rigorous with administrative follow-through, comfortable owning COI tracking, delivery scheduling, and request logs as a core, daily responsibility
Flexible availability, including occasional evenings/weekends for urgent issues
Willing to stay until the job is done, not a clock-watcher who hands off an unfinished task at the end of the day
Valid driver's license; comfort with occasional travel to Providence, RI as needed
Professional presentation and polish suited to high-end residential settings
Basic working knowledge of residential IT/AV and smart home systems is preferred but not required (e.g., Lutron, Crestron, Savant), comfortable handling simple troubleshooting, and knowing when to escalate to an AV vendor

Preferred Work Experience:

Background in hospitality, estate management, or luxury property services
Experience using property management systems
Deeper hands-on experience configuring or programming smart home/AV platforms (Lutron, Crestron, Savant) beyond basic use
Experience working alongside a PA/EA or household staff team in an integrated support model

Instills Trust -
Gaining the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity

Adapting approach and demeanor in real time to match the shifting demands of different situations
Action-Oriented-
Taking on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy, and enthusiasm

Building partnerships and working collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives
